correctness.rationale: After dihedral reduction, a unit base point is either a smooth point x=(c,t) on the reference edge or the endpoint vertex (c,s). For a smooth point the unique support functional forces y to the perpendicular edge midpoint, and the two chord norms are exactly sqrt(2) plus/minus t/(sqrt(2)c). At the vertex, the Birkhoff directions form the sector between the two perpendicular adjacent facet normals. On either half-edge of that sector the active chord facets remain the plus/minus pi/4 facets, giving sqrt(2) plus/minus (s-r)/(sqrt(2)c). These formulas exhaust all Birkhoff pairs and prove the pointwise straddling inequality. Quarter-turn vertex and edge-midpoint pairs attain equality.
risks: The proof uses the residue-class fact pi/4=2m alpha, so it does not automatically extend to other regular even polygons.
The numerical checker is supplementary; the continuum proof is the support-functional classification.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a single octagonal example into an infinite exact rigidity class and adds a pointwise theorem stronger than the two scalar constant identities. It shows that a large family of non-Hilbert polyhedral planes has Hilbert-valued orthogonal James and Schäffer constants for a structural residue-class reason, namely alignment of the quarter-diagonal with facet normals. This is a natural benchmark for how Birkhoff orthogonality can conceal non-Hilbert geometry.
risks: The complementary regular-polygon residue classes are not classified here.
